[id="troubleshooting-custom-ca-bundles_{context}"]
= Troubleshooting custom CA bundles

[role="_abstract"]
If you experience errors when configuring custom CA bundles for self-signed certificates, use the following information to resolve common issues and error messages.

If your issue is not described in the following information or in the release notes, contact {org-name} Support.

[id="common-issues_{context}"]
== Common issues

Certificate not found::
Ensure the config map exists in the expected namespace and contains the specified key.
To verify the config map and its keys, run the following command:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get configmap __<configmap-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ -o yaml
----
+
Confirm that the expected key, such as `ca-bundle.crt`, is displayed in the `data` section of the output.

Permission denied::
Check that the Llama Stack Operator service account has permissions to read the config map.
To verify the operator's permissions, run the following command:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc auth can-i get configmaps \
  --as=system:serviceaccount:__<operator-namespace>__:__<operator-sa-name>__ \
  -n __<configmap-namespace>__
----
+
To find the service account name that the Llama Stack Operator uses, run `oc get serviceaccounts -n __<operator-namespace>__`.
+
If the output is `no`, create a `Role` and `RoleBinding` in the config map namespace to grant the operator service account `get` access to config maps.

Invalid certificate::
Verify that the certificate is in valid Privacy-Enhanced Mail (PEM) format.
To validate a certificate file, run the following command:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ openssl x509 -text -noout -in __<certificate_file>__
----
+
If the command reports an error, the certificate is not valid PEM or is corrupted.

Pod not restarting::
When you update the `spec.server.tlsConfig.caBundle` field or the contents of the source config map, the Llama Stack Operator automatically updates the managed config map annotation, which triggers a pod rollout.
If the pod does not restart automatically, verify that the `LlamaStackDistribution` CR status does not report a validation error:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get llamastackdistribution __<instance-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ -o yaml
----
+
Check the `status.conditions` field for a `DeploymentReady` condition set to `"False"`.
If the CR status is healthy but the pod has not restarted, manually restart the deployment:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc rollout restart deployment/__<instance-name>__ -n __<namespace>__
----

[id="common-error-messages-and-solutions_{context}"]
== Common error messages and solutions

CA bundle key not found in ConfigMap::
+
.Problem
The specified key does not exist in the ConfigMap data.
+
.Resolution
Check the key name in your `LlamaStackDistribution` spec. The default key name is `ca-bundle.crt`. Run the following command and verify that your expected key is displayed in the output:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get configmap __<configmap-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ -o yaml
----

Invalid CA bundle format::
+
.Problem
The certificate data is not in valid PEM format or contains invalid certificates.
+
.Resolution
Ensure that each certificate is enclosed in `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----` and `-----END CERTIFICATE-----` markers (PEM format).
To verify the format, extract the certificate data from the config map and validate it:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get configmap __<configmap-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.ca-bundle\.crt}' > /tmp/ca-bundle.crt
$ openssl x509 -text -noout -in /tmp/ca-bundle.crt
----

Referenced CA bundle ConfigMap not found::
+
.Problem
The ConfigMap specified in `tlsConfig.caBundle.configMapName` does not exist.
+
.Resolution
Verify that the config map exists in the expected namespace:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get configmap __<configmap-name>__ -n __<namespace>__
----
+
If the config map does not exist, create it before applying the `LlamaStackDistribution` CR:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc create configmap __<configmap-name>__ \
  --from-file=ca-bundle.crt=__<path_to_ca_certificate>__ \
  -n __<namespace>__
----

No valid certificates found in CA bundle::
+
.Problem
The ConfigMap contains data but no parseable certificates.
+
.Resolution
Verify that the certificate file contains valid certificate data in PEM format.
To validate the certificate, run the following command:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ openssl x509 -text -noout -in __<certificate_file>__
----
+
If the certificate file is valid but the config map data is corrupted, re-create the config map with the correct certificate file.

Failed to parse certificate::
+
.Problem
Certificate data is corrupted or not a valid X.509 certificate.
+
.Resolution
Regenerate the certificate or verify the source.
Check that the certificate data is not double base64-encoded, which can occur when copying certificate content through intermediate tools.
To verify the encoding, extract and inspect the raw data:
+
[subs="+quotes"]
----
$ oc get configmap __<configmap-name>__ -n __<namespace>__ \
  -o jsonpath='{.data.ca-bundle\.crt}' | head -5
----
+
The first line of valid PEM data is `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`. If the output shows base64-encoded content without PEM markers, decode it first and re-create the config map.
